messages:
maria_h: Hey team — Solaria Health returned our vendor security form and has a couple of quick follow-ups before we finalize onboarding. I'm drafting responses but want to confirm a few infra/legal points so we don't misstate anything. TL;DR: questions on KMS (BYOK), SOC2 scope, and logs retention.
olivia_legal: Ok — quick flags:
- SOC2: our Type II covers the production inference runtime and the control plane for hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private, SOC2 applies to the parts we operate; customers can request evidence for private installs depending on hosting model.
- DPA: standard clause allows customer-managed keys for Dedicated via KMS integration. Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default.
sam_lee: Thanks. Customer specifically asked:
1) Can they supply their own key for encryption-at-rest on Dedicated? (they want BYOK)
2) Where are logs stored and for how long? They need to know if PII could appear in logs and retention policy.
tom_infra: Answers:
1) BYOK: yes on Dedicated — we support bringing your own KMS/HSM. Implementation details: customer provides key ARN (AWS) or key reference for GCP; we never export the key. Example: `kms:use_customer_key = true` in deployment config. For Private/on-prem, KMS is fully customer-managed.
2) Logs: application + inference logs for hosted are stored in our logs account (encrypted) for 90 days by default; access is limited to SRE & CS with audit. We can offer extended retention as an add-on. We scrub high-sensitivity tokens by default but recommend customers avoid sending unneeded PII in prompts.
olivia_legal: Add to DPA response: we need to make explicit that customer data may traverse the control plane for hosted deployments and that we have contractual obligations re: access. Also include our SOC2 letter and the last audit date. I'll attach the cert.
upload-bot: file uploaded: `redwood_soc2_type2_2025.pdf` (link: https://files.redwood.internal/soc2/2025)
maria_h: Perfect — I'll draft the reply to Solaria with the following bullets and send for legal review:
- Dedicated supports BYOK (how it works + caveats)
- Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default
- Logs retention: 90 days default; extended retention available via add-on
- SOC2 scope summary + attached cert
- Note: encourage they avoid embedding PII; we have prompt-scrubbing and suggest a design pattern
sam_lee: If you can paste the exact BYOK wording I'll include in the vendor form. Also, can we offer a line about data residency (they're EU-based)?
tom_infra: Data residency: Dedicated can be provisioned in EU region; hosted inference is available in our EU region and we can route requests to EU by policy. For DPA, specify region selection during provisioning. Short snippet: `data_residency: eu-west-1`.
maria_h: Thanks all. Olivia — can you add the one-sentence legal disclaimer about control plane traversal and I'll send draft to Solaria then post the final copy here. Targeting to reply today EOD. :thumbsup:
olivia_legal: Will do — sending the one-liner now.
olivia_legal: "Redwood processes customer content in the serving runtime and (for hosted customers) may transmit metadata through our control plane; access controls and audit logs limit internal access — see attached SOC2 report and DPA for full details." 
maria_h: Awesome, sending now. I'll update thread with their response and any follow-ups for enablement."
